places.quote: Mr. Tulkinghorn goes, as the crow came—not quite so straight, but nearly—to Cook’s Court, Cursitor Street.
places.note: Fictional-sounding court; a real Cook's Court off Cursitor Street existed, so located in Chancery Lane area.

places.quote: The middle-aged man in the pew knows scarcely more of the affairs of the peerage than any crossing-sweeper in Holborn.
Drafts that he requires to be drawn are drawn by special-pleaders in the temple on mysterious instructions;
places.note: Refers to the Inns of Court (the Temple).

places.normalized: Rule Office, Court of King's Bench, London
places.quote: he gives it in a written advertisement he sticks up down at the Rule Office, and the King’s Bench Office, and the Judges’ Chambers
